memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: 'then he is to take his wife to the priest. He must also take an offering of a tenth of an ephah of barley flour on her behalf. He must not pour olive oil on it or put incense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, an offering for remembrance to draw attention to wrongdoing.' - Num 5:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The suspicious husband could not simply act on his feelings; he had to bring the matter to the priest, and with it an offering. What was a private torment of jealousy was brought out into the open, into the presence of God, to be handled according to His way rather than the husband's impulse.

There is quiet wisdom in this. Jealousy and suspicion, left to fester in private, can drive a person to terrible things. By requiring the matter to be brought before God, this law refused to let dark suspicion be settled in the dark. It was dragged into the light, before the Lord.

We can learn from this pattern, even though the specific law is not for us today. When suspicion, jealousy, or a broken relationship torments us, the worst thing we can do is nurse it privately, replaying grievances and imagining the worst. The better way is to bring it into the light — before God in honest prayer, and, where wise, before trustworthy people who can help.

The offering here is called one "for remembrance." God does not overlook wrongdoing, but neither does He allow it to be dealt with by human rage. He calls it into His own presence.

Whatever secret worry or suspicion troubles your heart today, do not let it fester in the shadows. Bring it into the light of God's presence. Things handled before God are handled far better than things brooded over alone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you tend to nurse suspicions and worries in private?
- What would it mean to bring a troubling matter "before God"?
- How does the light of God's presence help us handle conflict?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when jealousy or suspicion troubles me, help me not to brood in the dark, but to bring everything into the light of Your presence. Amen.
